messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test "testGetLineNumberWithCR" is designed to check the line number tracking of CSVParser when the input consists of CR ('\r') as a line separator. The test creates a CSVParser with input containing 'a\rb\rc' and a CSVFormat using "\r" as the line separator, then asserts the line number is 1 after initialization.

The CSVParser.getLineNumber() delegates to lexer.getLineNumber(), which delegates to ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber(), which returns the internal lineCounter.

ExtendedBufferedReader overrides three read methods relevant to line counting:
- The single char read() increments lineCounter only on '\n'.
- The char array read() increments lineCounter on both '\r' and '\n', with some logic to avoid double-counting '\r\n'.
- The readLine() method delegates to BufferedReader.readLine() which normalizes EOLs (treats CR, LF, CRLF equally), but afterwards increments lineCounter unconditionally whenever a line is read.

The bug report points out a mismatch in handling line terminators between read() methods and readLine(). Specifically, read() only increments lineCounter on '\n', whereas read(char[], int, int) increments on both '\r' and '\n', and readLine() increments lineCounter for every line read using super.readLine() (which drops the line terminator).

Because the test uses "\r" as line separator (CR only), the read() method does not count '\r' as a line terminator and hence lineCounter may be off compared to what the format expects. The test expects line number to reflect the CR line separators, but ExtendedBufferedReader.read() does not increment lineCounter on '\r' so the resulting line number is wrong.

The root cause is the inconsistency in line counting among the read methods: read() only recognizes '\n', read(char[], int, int) correctly recognizes both '\r' and '\n', but readLine() increments lineCounter based on the number of lines read without considering CR-only line separators distinctly.

This behavior causes line number tracking to be inconsistent and fail the test when CR is the only line separator.

Recent bug reports about line terminator handling and escaping do not conflict with this diagnosis. The current bug report directly describes this line terminator counting mismatch in ExtendedBufferedReader.

Hence, the bug is in ExtendedBufferedReader where read() does not increment lineCounter on '\r', causing inconsistent line number tracking when only CR is used as EOL.

# Summary:
- Test uses CR as line separator.
- ExtendedBufferedReader.read() increments lineCounter only on '\n', not on '\r'.
- read(char[],int,int) increments lineCounter on both '\r' and '\n'.
- readLine() increments lineCounter for each line read but uses super.readLine() which treats CR homogeneously, plus increments lineCounter once per line regardless.
- This inconsistency leads to wrong line number reported by CSVParser.
- Fix involves making sure ExtendedBufferedReader.read() also increments lineCounter on '\r' to be consistent.

This explains why testGetLineNumberWithCR() fails (line number is incorrect) as ExtendedBufferedReader does not handle '\r' consistently in all read methods.

---

Next, I will suggest which methods are suitable for the fix.
org.apache.commons.csv.ExtendedBufferedReader.read()
org.apache.commons.csv.ExtendedBufferedReader.readLine()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
